request.spec: The people, claims and pools exports taken while an as-of date is set use the as-of figures.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The people, claims and pools exports taken while an as-of date is set use the as-of figures.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Exports taken while an as-of date is set now use the as-of figures. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests, including the "as of exports" test that failed before the change.

**What was wrong:** the server already answers reads with the as-of data. The exports are built in the browser from data the screen has already loaded. When you set an as-of date, the "As of" label updated straight away, but the screen was still clearing and re-reading the people, claims, pools and settings. An export clicked in that window came out with only the header line (the test got exactly that).

**The fix (front end only):**
- `core/session.ts` now keeps track of the sheet's re-reads that are still running: the sheet load itself, plus anything a loader registers with the new `reading()`. A new `settled()` waits until all of them have finished.
- The people loader (`features/people/people.ts`), the pools store (`features/pools/pools-api.ts`) and the settings loader (`features/settings/settings.ts`) now register their reads that way.
- The people, claims and pools exports first wait for `settled()` and then build the CSV. So the file always reflects what the screen is showing: the as-of figures while a date is set, and the current figures once it is cleared.

Other screens that reload when a sheet loads (rates, periods, plans and so on) don't register yet; only the loaders these exports read from do. The server and the stored data needed no change.
